overview.title: Sea and mountain in one park
overview.p1: Al Hoceima National Park protects a stretch of Mediterranean cliff coast and nearshore waters west of town. Limestone headlands, hidden coves and marine life are the core of the landscape.
overview.p2: Come for viewpoints, short coastal walks and a sense of how steeply the Rif meets the sea. Cala Iris and Torres de Alcalá sit in or beside this protected shoreline.
overview.p3: Wear steady shoes, carry water and respect any marked paths or access rules — this is a conservation area, not a city beach.

faq.title: أسئلة شائعة حول المنتزه الوطني للحسيمة

q1.question: Do I need a guide?
q1.answer: Not for main viewpoints; useful for longer trails or boat approaches to remote coves.

q2.question: Can I swim in the park?
q2.answer: Some coves allow swimming; check local conditions and any seasonal rules.

q3.question: Best season for hiking?
q3.answer: Spring and autumn for milder temperatures on exposed cliffs.

q4.question: How far from town?
q4.answer: Trailheads and park coast sites are a drive west — confirm times with a taxi or tour.

q5.question: Is it suitable for children?
q5.answer: Viewpoints yes; longer cliff paths need care and proper footwear.
